title: What is Field Operations Management?
summary: Field Operations Management names the category for running, recording, and closing out physical field work. See what it covers.
body_markdown:
What is Field Operations Management?


**


Field Operations Management (FOM) is the discipline of running, recording, and closing out the physical work field teams do. It covers the full lifecycle of an asset or work order, from first site visit to final record. Operations teams get real-time visibility into field status, location, documentation, and closeout progress along the way. Safety and compliance requirements travel with every job from the first step to the last.


What kinds of work fall under Field Operations Management?


**


Field Operations Management (FOM) covers four categories of physical work that look very different on paper:


- Asset installation and maintenance, covering the records crews generate while installing, servicing, and tracking equipment over time
- Vegetation management and environmental surveys, which turn tree trimming and hazard tree assessments into structured records at closeout
- Site inspection and construction closeout, keeping pre-construction inspections, as-built data, and final documentation tied to one job record
- Disaster recovery and compliance documentation, holding emergency response paperwork to the same audit standard as routine maintenance


Underneath, every category does the same job: turning fieldwork into a record someone else can trust.


What does a Field Operations Management platform include?


**


A Field Operations Management platform covers work orders, standardized forms and inspection checklists, GPS-verified records, offline capture, real-time job status, and closeout reporting. What separates it from a set of point solutions is that all of it shares one data model, so a record captured in the field is reportable without a cleanup pass. Our[Field Operations Management primer](https://www.fulcrumapp.com/primers/field-operations-management/) walks through each capability in depth.


Why do customer service, GIS, and construction platforms fall short for Field Operations Management?


**


Most teams stretch three types of software across field operations and fill the gaps with spreadsheets and paper. Customer service platforms schedule appointments and track service-level agreements for work performed on behalf of paying customers. Systems of record, including geographic information system (GIS), asset management, and financial platforms, each store one slice of the record. Construction platforms stop at handoff, which is exactly when the asset’s working life begins. Each tool does its own job well, and the gaps between them are where field data goes missing.


What are the hidden costs of disconnected field operations?


**


Running field operations on disconnected tools creates three costs, starting with delayed closeout on completed assets. On capital programs, closing out a finished asset can trail construction by weeks or months. The asset earns no return during that entire stretch, even though the crew finished the physical work long before. Scattered records create the second cost, forcing crews to re-collect data that already exists in another system. Small errors slip in with every re-collection and often stay hidden until an audit surfaces them as violations. The third cost is lost knowledge, because veteran fieldworkers carry judgment that retires with them unless a system captures it.


How is Field Operations Management different from field service management?


**


Field service software is built around a customer call. Field Operations Management is built around an asset or a work order, so the job starts at a location rather than a customer, and the record it produces has to hold up in an audit years later. We compare the two categories in[FSM vs. FOM platforms](https://www.fulcrumapp.com/resources/) .


Why does AI in field operations need a dedicated platform?


**


Artificial intelligence (AI) needs consistent, structured data, and most field data sits in paper forms, PDFs, and spreadsheets. A Field Operations Management platform produces structured data as crews do the work, so every record arrives AI-ready. Because the platform captures the whole field job continuously, AI gets the complete picture to reason over. Fieldworkers also carry the platform on every job, so AI assistance reaches them at the point of work. Customers using Fulcrum’s AI-native platform report 30% fewer hours managing and quality-checking field data.


How does a Field Operations Management platform handle GIS and location data?


**


Location is built into a Field Operations Management platform, so every record carries spatial context the moment it’s captured. Teams view each record on a map immediately, with no round-trip through a separate geographic information system (GIS). Integration runs in both directions, pulling asset records and work orders in and pushing completed work back to GIS. Workflows also include offline use and reliable sync, so crews capture location-tagged records even where coverage drops out.


How does a Field Operations Management platform improve safety?


**


A Field Operations Management platform builds safety steps into the same workflow crews use to complete the job. Safety checks happen at the point of work and get recorded alongside the rest of the job data. Safety and compliance requirements travel with the job from the first site visit through final closeout. Each completed check becomes part of the job’s auditable record, ready when an inspector or auditor asks for it.


Can field teams build their own workflows on a Field Operations Management platform?


**


Field Operations Management platforms allow field teams to build their on workflows. On Fulcrum’s Field Operations Management platform, teams build the workflows they need to fit the job. No-code tools let admins drag fields and logic into forms that match how the work gets done. Teams that need more can add data events and integrations, or use AI to build custom extensions. Every workflow automatically includes offline use, reliable sync, and geographic information system (GIS) integration, so builders never start from scratch. Changes stay in the hands of the people who manage the fieldwork, with no development queue in between.
